Kastamonu (preceding the Candars) 1211–1309'), then Candar land. This dossier takes years 1309-1313 of the 1305 shape (19,765 km2) and joins them to the Eflani shape: the Candar realm after Süleyman I's conquest. Page gives no area or boundary.

The page gives no boundary; the Candar page says the realm reigned 'under the authority of the Ilkhanate' until Abu Sa'id's death (1335).

The page has no area.

48,841 km2: Cliopatria folds its Kastamonu row into the Isfendiyar row in 1344 (120 of the 150 added cells are Kastamonu's) and adds 30 cells (about 8,300 km2) round Çankırı and Tosya in the south. The Candar page lists the provinces 'Eflani, Kastamonu, Sinop, Zonguldak, Bartın, Karabük, Samsun, Bolu, Ankara and Çankırı' and gives no area in km2, so no infobox ratio. Timur later 'confirmed İsfendiyar's rule in the traditional Candar realm of Kastamonu, Kalecik, Tosya, and Çankırı' (1402), which fits the southern lobe, but no page dates its acquisition.
49,010 km2: three cells change owner with the Ottoman Empire at the southern edge (grid noise); no page explains a change in 1363. Unverified: page budget.

48,962 km2, 48 km2 less than 1363 (grid noise); no event. The page records a split in the dynasty in 1383 ('lost Kastamonu to one of his own sons, Süleyman'; Kötürüm Bayezid 'retreated to Sinop, which led to the division of the Beylik of Candar') which Cliopatria does not draw; the realm was reunited under Süleyman II in 1385.

Years only: unchanged shape, valid 1385-1390. Cliopatria runs it to 1401 but 'In 1391 ... Bayezid I launched an assault on Kastamonu', which 'saw the death of Süleyman II and with it an end to the Candar dynasty's long reign in Kastamonu'; İsfendiyar 'recognized the suzerainty of Bayezid I and became an Ottoman vassal' (Candar page). The Kastamonu country is Ottoman from 1391 to 1402; see the next keyframe.

correction.text: the Sinop country, the part of the Candar realm that stayed with İsfendiyar as an Ottoman vassal

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: the realm less the Kastamonu country, 1391-1401: the Sinop country (50 cells, 13,622 km2) stays with İsfendiyar as an Ottoman vassal, and the infobox moves the capital to Sinop in 1398. The page does not say what the Ottomans held beyond Kastamonu; the southern lobe (Çankırı) is assumed lost with it (confidence 2). Bayezid I page: after the 1391 peace with Karaman he 'moved north against Kastamonu' and 'conquered both that city as well as Sinop'; the Candar page instead leaves İsfendiyar at Sinop as an autonomous Ottoman vassal, which this keyframe follows (pages disagree; reviewer me-09-e).

49,106 km2 for 1402-1406, one cell more than 1385 (grid noise). 'after Bayezid was defeated at the hands of the Timurids in 1402, İsfendiyar recognized the authority of their Khan, Timur, who confirmed İsfendiyar's rule in the traditional Candar realm of Kastamonu, Kalecik, Tosya, and Çankırı' (Candar page): the whole realm is back.

Years only: 49,010 km2 for 1407-1458. Candar page: 'Kasım claimed control over Çankırı and Tosya and declared the incorporation of these provinces to the Ottoman Empire'; İsfendiyar then 'revolted against the new sultan Murad II, only to be defeated, and retreated to Sinop in 1423'. Battle of Bolu page: he 'took Tosya, Çankırı, and Kalecik from them' while Murad II was occupied (1421-1423) and was defeated at Bolu in 1423; the Ottomans then occupied Küre and he sent his son to ask for peace, terms not given. So the lobe is Ottoman for an undated stretch before 1422 (drawn as 1421 only, confidence 1) and Candar again from 1422 (pages silent on any later loss).

Years only: unchanged shape, valid 1459-1461. Cliopatria runs it to 1462; the Candar page ends the dynasty in 1461 ('In 1461 ... he captured Sinop', Mehmed II; infobox 'Ended: 1461'). Cliopatria's Ottoman shape takes the land in 1463.

region.text: the province of Eflani, with Safranbolu

ledger.note: 1291: Şemseddin Yaman Candar Bey founds the Candar principality at Eflani. Infobox 'Founded: 1291, by Şemseddin Yaman Candar Bey'; the Seljuk sultan 'awarded the province of Eflani to Şemseddin Yaman Candar'. The page gives the province, not a boundary.

1309: Süleyman I takes Kastamonu from the Chobanids. 'his son Süleyman I conquered the neighboring province of Kastamonu' (undated; the infobox moves the capital to Kastamonu in 1309 and the beyliks table ends the Chobanid beylik in 1309). 'The province had previously been under the rule of the Çobanoğulları.'
1309: the Candar seat moves from Eflani to Kastamonu (infobox 'Eflani 1291–1309; Kastamonu 1309–1398').

region.text: Eflani and the Kastamonu country, the Candar realm of Süleyman I, under Ilkhanid authority

ledger.note: 1309: Süleyman I rules Kastamonu under Ilkhanid authority. Candar page: 'Süleyman reigned under the authority of the Ilkhanate, the Mongols of Persia, until the death of their ruler Abu Sa'id.' The page gives no year for the start of the relation; 1309 is the conquest of Kastamonu (infobox capital 'Kastamonu 1309–1398'). The ilkhanate dossier carries the same vassalage from 1305 under the Cliopatria rows kastamonu and beylik-of-sinop; the Candar page makes the vassal this state.

region.text: the Sinop country, the Pervâneid emirate annexed by Süleyman I

ledger.note: 1322: the Candars annex Sinop from the Pervâneids. The Candar page says Süleyman I 'annexed Safranbolu and Sinop' (no year); the beyliks table gives 'Pervâneid | Sinop | 1277–1322', which fixes the year. Safranbolu already lies in the Eflani shape.

region.text: the Candar realm of Eflani, Kastamonu and Sinop

ledger.note: 30 November 1335: the Ilkhanid authority ends with Abu Said. Candar page: Süleyman reigned under Ilkhanid authority 'until the death of their ruler Abu Sa'id' (no year on that page); Abu Sa'id page: 'died on his way in Karabakh on the night of 30 November 1335' (the infobox says 1 December).

region.text: the southern lobe round Çankırı and Tosya, added to the shape in 1344

ledger.note: 1344 (page silent): Cliopatria adds about 30 cells (8,300 km2) in the south, round Çankırı and Tosya, to the Candar shape. No page dates the acquisition; Timur confirmed 'Kastamonu, Kalecik, Tosya, and Çankırı' as the traditional realm in 1402 (confidence 1).

region.text: the Kastamonu country and the south (Kastamonu, Kalecik, Tosya, Çankırı), the realm less the Sinop country

ledger.note: 1391: Bayezid I takes Kastamonu. 'In 1391, Murad's successor to the Ottoman throne, Bayezid I, launched an assault on Kastamonu', which 'saw the death of Süleyman II and with it an end to the Candar dynasty's long reign in Kastamonu'; İsfendiyar 'recognized the suzerainty of Bayezid I and became an Ottoman vassal'. Which towns beyond Kastamonu fell is not on the page.

region.text: the Sinop country, the part of the Candar realm that stayed with İsfendiyar

ledger.note: 1391: İsfendiyar, left at Sinop, becomes an Ottoman vassal. Candar page: after Bayezid I's assault on Kastamonu İsfendiyar 'recognized the suzerainty of Bayezid I and became an Ottoman vassal' (no separate year). The Bayezid I page instead has Bayezid conquer 'both that city as well as Sinop'; the two pages disagree and this entry follows the Candar page.
1398: the Candar seat is Sinop (infobox 'Sinop 1398–1461'; the body gives no year for the move).

region.text: the traditional Candar realm of Kastamonu, Kalecik, Tosya and Çankırı

ledger.note: 1402: Timur confirms İsfendiyar in Kastamonu, Kalecik, Tosya and Çankırı. 'after Bayezid was defeated at the hands of the Timurids in 1402, İsfendiyar recognized the authority of their Khan, Timur, who confirmed İsfendiyar's rule in the traditional Candar realm of Kastamonu, Kalecik, Tosya, and Çankırı.' Battle of Ankara: 20 July 1402 (Bayezid I page).

region.text: the Sinop country, the part of the Candar realm that stayed with İsfendiyar

ledger.note: 1402: the Ottoman suzerainty ends with the defeat at Ankara. Candar page: 'after Bayezid was defeated at the hands of the Timurids in 1402, İsfendiyar recognized the authority of their Khan, Timur' (Battle of Ankara 20 July 1402, Bayezid I page).

region.text: Kastamonu, Kalecik, Tosya and Çankırı with the Sinop country: the Candar realm Timur confirmed

ledger.note: 1402: İsfendiyar recognizes Timur. Candar page: İsfendiyar 'recognized the authority of their Khan, Timur, who confirmed İsfendiyar's rule in the traditional Candar realm of Kastamonu, Kalecik, Tosya, and Çankırı.' The month is not given.

1403 (a bridge over a silence): Timur leaves Anatolia. The Candar page says only that 'Following the departure of Timur from Anatolia during the Ottoman Interregnum' İsfendiyar stood close to Bayezid's four sons, with no year; 1403 is the year the timurid-empire dossier ends the Anatolian occupation (confidence 1 there too; Timur's camp at Birtvisi in August 1403 on the Georgia page).

region.text: the southern lobe, Çankırı, Tosya and Kalecik (Candar page: 'Çankırı and Tosya'; Battle of Bolu page: 'Tosya, Çankırı and Kalecik')

ledger.note: By 1421 (latest year the pages allow; the true year is not given): Çankırı and Tosya are Ottoman. Candar page: 'Kasım claimed control over Çankırı and Tosya and declared the incorporation of these provinces to the Ottoman Empire', after the Interregnum and before İsfendiyar 'revolted against the new sultan Murad II' (accession 1421, Battle of Bolu page). The Mehmed I page has a 'Kıvameddin Kazim Bey, son of Isfendyar Bey' (probably the Candar page's Kasım; an identification of mine) marry into Mehmed I's family (entry of Fatma Sultan Hatun) and its infobox lists 'Conquest of Candar dynasty' without a year, so the real date may lie earlier, in Mehmed I's reign; 1421 keeps the unverified Ottoman hold as short as the pages allow. Kalecik is added from the Battle of Bolu page.

region.text: the southern lobe, Çankırı, Tosya and Kalecik (Candar page: 'Çankırı and Tosya'; Battle of Bolu page: 'Tosya, Çankırı and Kalecik')

ledger.note: 1422 (a bridge inside 1421-1423): İsfendiyar retakes the lobe. Battle of Bolu page: while Murad II was occupied with the rebellion of Mustafa Çelebi (accession 1421, execution 20 February 1423), 'İsfendiyar Bey ... took Tosya, Çankırı, and Kalecik from them'; no year for the seizure. The 1423 battle is dated by the Candar and Battle of Bolu pages; the page gives no terms of the peace he asked for, so the lobe is kept to 1461.

region.text: the whole principality: Kastamonu, Sinop, Çankırı and the coast

ledger.note: 1461: Mehmed II takes Sinop and ends the Candar dynasty. 'In 1461, joining forces with Ismail's brother Kızıl Ahmed Bey, he captured Sinop' and 'officially ended the reign of the Candar dynasty'; 'Kızıl Ahmed Bey ruled for three months before the principality's incorporation into the Ottoman Empire.' The Mehmed II page has the summer-1461 campaign (Trebizond fell on 15 August 1461).

1461: the Candar principality is incorporated into the Ottoman Empire (infobox 'Ended: 1461'; 'Succeeded by: Ottoman Empire'). Kızıl Ahmed Bey's governorship of Kastamonu and Sinop was 'revoked in 1464'.

wars.name: Bayezid I's assault on Kastamonu
wars.outcome: Süleyman II dies and the Candar reign in Kastamonu ends; İsfendiyar, at Sinop, accepts Bayezid's suzerainty as a vassal. The Candar realm returns in 1402 under Timur.
wars.note: Bayezid I page: after the 1391 peace with Karaman he 'moved north against Kastamonu' and 'conquered both that city as well as Sinop' (the Candar page leaves Sinop to İsfendiyar as a vassal); his later campaign was halted by Kadi Burhan al-Din at Kırkdilim (20 July 1391 on the Ertuğrul Çelebi entry of that page). The Candar page says 1391 for the assault.

wars.name: Battle of Ankara and the Timurid confirmation of İsfendiyar
wars.outcome: Timur defeats Bayezid I and confirms İsfendiyar's rule in Kastamonu, Kalecik, Tosya and Çankırı.
wars.note: The restoration is the ledger's 1402 gain; no border is contested.

wars.name: İsfendiyar's revolt against Murad II and the Battle of Bolu

zones.text: the southern lobe, Çankırı, Tosya and Kalecik (Candar page: 'Çankırı and Tosya'; Battle of Bolu page: 'Tosya, Çankırı and Kalecik')

wars.outcome: While Murad II was occupied with Mustafa Çelebi (accession 1421, execution 20 February 1423), İsfendiyar took Tosya, Çankırı and Kalecik from the Ottomans (Battle of Bolu page); in 1423 Murad II defeated the Candar army at Bolu, near Safranbolu, where Kasım Bey's Ottoman force made Candar troops defect; İsfendiyar, wounded, 'retreated to Sinop in 1423' (Candar page), Ottoman troops occupied Küre, and he sent his son Murad to propose peace; the terms are not on the page.
wars.note: Candar page: Kasım 'claimed control over Çankırı and Tosya and declared the incorporation of these provinces to the Ottoman Empire' before the revolt. Murad II married İsfendiyar's kin, Hatice Halime Hatun, in 1425 (Murad II page); the Murad II page names no land. Küre is not drawn: the page does not say the Ottomans kept it.

wars.name: Mehmed II's conquest of Sinop and the Candar principality
wars.outcome: Mehmed II, with İsmail's brother Kızıl Ahmed Bey, captures Sinop and ends the Candar dynasty in the summer campaign of 1461; the principality is incorporated into the Ottoman Empire.
wars.note: Mehmed II page: he 'captured Sinope and ended the official reign of the Jandarid dynasty' in the summer 1461 campaign that also took Trebizond (15 August 1461).

certainty.note: No page opened gives a treaty line or survey; the Black Sea, Çankırı and Bolu frontiers are approximate throughout.

notes:
Row identity (two Cliopatria rows, one state): the Cliopatria row 'Beylik of Isfendiyar' (Wikipedia 'Candar dynasty', Q2096678, Seshat tr_candar_bey) is the Candar principality at Eflani and its whole life to 1461; the 'Kastamonu' row's shapes from 1309 are Candar land, as the kastamonu dossier asked (it keeps the Chobanid beylik 1211-1309 only), so 'Kastamonu' is listed in cliopatria_names and its three shapes are reviewed here (kastamonu_1305 for 1309-1313, kastamonu_1314 for 1314-1321, kastamonu_1333 marked as an alias of beylik-of-isfendiyar_1333). Cliopatria's 'Beylik of Sinop' (same Wikidata Q2096678) is the Pervâneid emirate of Sinop 1277-1322, a different state that the Candars annexed in 1322 (beylik-of-sinop dossier; table row 'Pervâneid | Sinop | 1277–1322'), so it is not merged here.
Dates: the page's founding is 1291 (Cliopatria row from 1305) and its end 1461 (Cliopatria 1462; Cliopatria's Ottoman shape takes the land in 1463, so the ottoman-empire dossier's 1462 gain is a year late). No page gives an area in km2 (the infobox lists provinces), so no ratio.
Page budget (up to 5): Candar dynasty (three questions), Anatolian beyliks (two), Bayezid I, Mehmed II. Not settled: the date of the Kastamonu conquest (Süleyman I's succession, 1309 from the infobox capital and the beyliks table's Chobanid end); the date of the southern lobe (Çankırı, Tosya, Kalecik: undated); whether the Ottomans held anything beyond Kastamonu 1391-1402 (confidence 2); the 1383 division of the dynasty (Kötürüm Bayezid at Sinop, Süleyman at Kastamonu) and its reunion in 1385 (not territorial); infobox capital Kastamonu to 1398 against Süleyman II's death there in 1391.
Cross-dossier for the orchestrator: (1) the ilkhanate dossier names beylik-of-sinop and kastamonu as its vassals 1305-1335; the Candar page puts Süleyman I 'under the authority of the Ilkhanate ... until the death of their ruler Abu Sa'id', so the vassal counterpart from 1309 should be beylik-of-isfendiyar. (2) The ottoman-empire dossier (me-10) has no gain for Kastamonu in 1391 and no loss in 1402; its 1462 gain should be 1461 and its source for Sinop/Kastamonu can cite the Candar page. (3) The kastamonu dossier already mirrors the 1309 loss. (4) beylik-of-sinop's 1322 loss to beylik-of-isfendiyar is mirrored here. (5) Gazetteer: Eflani, Safranbolu, Tosya and Kalecik are not in places.jsonl; shapes are cited by Cliopatria year instead.
Fix pass (author, reviewer me-09-e): (1) The Candar page does name a land change before 1423: Kasım 'claimed control over Çankırı and Tosya' for the Ottomans; the Battle of Bolu page adds that İsfendiyar 'took Tosya, Çankırı, and Kalecik from them' while Murad II was occupied (1421-1423). Neither dates the Ottoman hold. I record a loss in 1421 (the latest year the pages allow) and a gain in 1422, both at confidence 1 (the reviewer proposed confidence 2 and 1423; I disagree on both: with the Bolu page the lobe is back with İsfendiyar by the 1423 battle, and the year of the Ottoman acquisition is on no page; the Mehmed I page's infobox 'Conquest of Candar dynasty' and a Kazim Bey, son of Isfendyar, in that family suggest the true date lies in Mehmed I's reign, so the Ottoman hold is probably longer than drawn). Keyframes 1407 (adjust, years) and a new one-year keyframe 1421; the war now has the lobe as its zone. The Ottoman occupation of Küre after Bolu is not drawn (no terms, no extent). (2) Vassal events added at confidence 2 (1 for the bridging end): ilkhanate 1309-1335 (Candar page 'until the death of ... Abu Sa'id'; death 30 November 1335, Abu Sa'id page), ottoman-empire 1391-1402 (the Sinop country; 'became an Ottoman vassal'), timurid-empire 1402-1403 (the whole realm; 1403 is the timurid-empire dossier's year for Timur leaving Anatolia, the Candar page gives none). The ilkhanate dossier still names kastamonu and beylik-of-sinop as its 1309-1335 vassals (route to ia-02). (3) Thin items reopened: the date of the southern lobe is not on the Çankırı page; the 1383 division is on the Candar page ('Kötürüm Bayezid Bey retreated to Sinop, which led to the division of the Beylik of Candar'; 1385: 'On Kötürüm Bayezid's death in 1385, his son Süleyman succeeded him as Süleyman II', who 'remained faithful to Murad I') but is a split inside the dynasty and not drawn. The infobox/body years for İsfendiyar's reign differ (table 1385-1440, text 'died in 1439'). The ottoman-empire dossier (me-10) needs the 1421 gain and 1422 loss of the lobe, and the 1391 vassal of Sinop.
